1528.t: From ἀλέξω (ăléxō, “to repel”) + ἀνδρ- (ăndr-, stem of ἀνήρ (ănḗr, “man”)) + -ος (-os), literally “man who repels [enemies]”.

1527.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ántʰos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éndʰos. Cognate with Vedic Sanskrit अन्धस् (ándhas, “Soma, grass, herb”), Albanian endë, Old Armenian անդ (and, “field”), possibly Old Frisian åndul.

1554.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *nebʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *nébʰos Proto-Hellenic *népʰos Ancient Greek νέφος From Proto-Hellenic *népʰos, from Proto-Indo-European *nébʰos (“cloud”).

1533.t: From ἐξίστημι (exístēmi, “to displace”) from ἐκ (ek, “out”) and ἵστημι (hístēmi, “to stand”).

1502.t: Borrowed from Old Persian 𐎢𐎳𐎼𐎠𐎬𐎢 (u-f-r-a-tu-u /⁠ʰUfrātuš⁠/), from Akkadian 𒀀𒇉𒌓𒄒𒉣 (^(ÍD<)pu-rat-tu), itself from Sumerian 𒀀𒇉𒌓𒄒𒉣 (^(ÍD)Buranun). Cognates include Hebrew פְּרָת (pərāṯ) and Elamite 𒌑𒅁𒊏𒌅𒅖 (ú-ip-ra-du-iš).

1503.t: From βαθύς (bathús, “deep”) + -ος (-os), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʷeh₂dʰ- (“to sink, submerge”) (though Beekes rejects the link to the Indo-European root).

1514.t: From Proto-Hellenic *koňňós, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱomyós, from *ḱóm (“with”) + *-yós (“adjectival suffix”), the ancestor of the suffix -ιος (-ios). Cognates include Latin cum, Gaulish com-, and Old English ge-.

1523.t: From the root of σκέπτομαι (sképtomai, “to observe”) + -ός (-ós).

1575.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ennéwə, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁néwn̥. Cognates include Old Armenian ինն (inn), Sanskrit नव (náva), Latin novem, and Old English nigon (English nine).

1538.t: Explained since antiquity as a compound of αἴθω (aíthō, “to burn”) + ὤψ (ṓps, “face”), though this is generally thought to be a folk etymology.

1542.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵem- (“to marry”). Cognate with Sanskrit जामातृ (jā́mātṛ), Avestan 𐬰𐬁𐬨𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭 (zāmātar).

1536.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ortʰwós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃r̥dʰwós, from *h₃erdʰ- (“upright”). Cognate with Latin arduus, Sanskrit ऊर्ध्व (ūrdhvá).

1513.t: According to Beekes, acquired from Pre-Greek. Said Pre-Greek term may be ultimately derived from or at least related to Proto-Hurro-Urartian *kinnar (“lyre, harp”).

1568.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aywetós, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewyetós, from *h₂éwis (“bird”). Cognate with Sanskrit वि (ví), Latin avis, Old Armenian հաւ (haw).

1577.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *h₁er-, with cognates including Latin ariēs (“ram”), Old Irish heirp, erb (“kid”), and Lithuanian ė́ras (“lamb”), but more likely of substrate origin (along with the Latin and Old Irish) in view of the strange suffixes…

1579.t: From Proto-Indo-European *werǵ- (“work”), formed similarly to ξόανον (xóănon, “statue, xoanon”); compare ἔργον (érgon, “work, deed”).

1594.t: Likely from a Proto-Indo-European *mel- (“limb”); compare Breton mell (“joint”), Cornish mal (“id”), Welsh cymmal (“id”), which are from Proto-Celtic *melsā (“knuckle”).

1558.t: From Proto-Indo-European *péth₂eti (“to fly”), from the root *peth₂- (literally “to spread one’s wings”).

1504.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷiā, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷey- (“to win”). Cognate with Sanskrit ज्या (jyā́, “overwhelming force; power; vanquishing”), ज॒य (jayá, “victory”).

1524.t: From Proto-Hellenic *státis, from Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂tis (whence also Latin statiō, Gothic 𐍃𐍄𐌰𐌸𐍃 (staþs, “place”), and Old English stede (English stead)), from *steh₂- (“to stand”).

1557.t: From earlier *ποικιλός (*poikilós), with retraction of the accent by Wheeler's law; from Proto-Indo-European *peyḱ- (“to mark, embroider, color, paint”) + -λός (-lós).

1560.t: Though traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to be stiff; post”) (compare Sanskrit स्तम्भ (stambha, “pillar”), Old English stæf (“staff”)) via an assumed intermediate sense “stem”, according to Beekes, the word is clearly Pre-Greek,…

1521.t: From πλέον (pléon, “too much”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

1516.t: Of uncertain origin, though perhaps related to λιμός (līmós, “famine”) (via ablaut), as well as λοιγός (loigós, “ruin”) (via different suffix). Compare λύμη (lū́mē), λῦμα (lûmă), λυμαίνομαι (lūmaínomai)

1509.t: Back-formation from θηράω (thēráō, “to hunt”). Compare Tocharian B śerwe (“hunter”).

1572.t: Etymology tree Proto-Hellenic *akā́ Ancient Greek ἀκή (akḗ) Proto-Indo-European *h₂endʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *h₂éndʰos Proto-Hellenic *ántʰos Ancient Greek ἄνθος (ánthos) Pre-Greek? Ancient Greek ἄκανθα Traditionally derived from…

1580.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + indefinite που (pou). Compare οὗ (hoû).

1596.t: From προσ- (pros-, “to, towards, with”) + καλέω (kaléō, “to call”).

1567.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰh₂- (“to come near, nearly reach, pass”), and cognate with a Sanskrit धग्नु (dhagnu). However, such a Sanskrit term does not seem to be attested in Sanskrit dictionaries.

1511.t: κατα- (kata-, strengthening prefix) + σκευάζω (skeuázō, “equip”), from σκευή (skeuḗ, “equipment”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

1555.t: Mediopassive form (with perfective meaning?) to Ancient Greek οἰχνέω (oikhnéō, “to go, come, walk, approach”), both connected to Armenian and Tocharian verbal forms (with meanings such as Old Armenian իջանեմ (iǰanem, “to come down”) and Tocharian B yku…

1562.t: From ταράσσω (tărắssō, “to disturb; to stir; to agitate”) + -ή (-ḗ).

1584.t: From γέννα (génna, “descent, birth, origin”) + -ιος (-ios). Compare ἀγενής (agenḗs).

1515.t: Possibly from a Proto-Hellenic *kū́ros + -όω (-óō). Related to κύριος (kúrios).

1534.t: The verb is clearly related to Old Armenian եփեմ (epʻem, “to boil, cook”) (whence modern Armenian եփել (epʻel)).

1539.t: From Biblical Hebrew נִינְוֵה (Nînwê), from Akkadian 𒌷𒀏𒆠 (Ninua).
